items.headline: ILLIT scores first Billboard 200 top 10 with ‘BREAK EVEN’
items.dek: The mini album also gives the group its first No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Album Sales chart.
body: ILLIT has landed its first top 10 album on the Billboard 200, as “BREAK EVEN” debuts at No. 6 on the U.S. chart dated November 14.
The mini album also opens at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Album Sales chart, marking the group’s first release to lead the sales ranking, Soompi reported.

According to Luminate, “BREAK EVEN” earned 37,000 equivalent album units in the United States during the week ending November 5. That total included 32,500 traditional album sales, ILLIT’s biggest U.S. sales week to date, and 4,500 streaming equivalent album units. The latter represented 4.87 million on-demand audio streams.
The Billboard 200 ranks albums using a combination of sales and streaming activity, while Top Album Sales measures album sales. Billboard announced the new chart results on November 8.

“BREAK EVEN” is ILLIT’s fifth Billboard 200 entry and surpasses the group’s previous peak of No. 26 with “MAMIHLAPINATAPAI.” Their other entries were “SUPER REAL ME,” which reached No. 93; “I’LL LIKE YOU,” which peaked at No. 94; and “bomb,” which reached No. 171.

items.headline: Joy and Kim Hyun Jin Get Off to a Rocky Start in ‘One-of-a-Kind Romance’
items.dek: Repeated encounters leave a job seeker under suspicion by a top star in the webtoon-based drama’s first two episodes.
body: Red Velvet’s Joy and Kim Hyun Jin are set to begin their romance on the wrong foot in “One-of-a-Kind Romance,” which releases its first two episodes on November 9 at 6 p.m. KST.

Joy plays Gong Yu Il, a college graduate trying to find a job while working to support herself. Even on the day of an interview, she takes a night shift at a convenience store. There, she meets customer Tak Mu I, a top star played by Kim Hyun Jin.

The pair cross paths again at a filming location, but what feels like coincidence to Yu Il looks more suspicious to Mu I. Already stressed by a stalker, he begins to keep an eye on her. When he spots her on set, he exchanges a telling glance with his manager, Kim Young Soo, played by Choi Kwon.

Yu Il’s friend Yoo Yeon Joo, a drama production PD played by Na Hyun Young, also appears in the opening episodes. Yu Il eventually becomes Mu I’s manager, bringing the two closer as they develop a relationship. Mu I, who carries emotional scars from the stalking incident, once found strength in a novel Yu Il wrote years earlier.
Based on a Naver webtoon by Dubu, the drama is directed by Kim Jin Young and written by Jeon Hyun Mi. The first two episodes will be available on TVING, Viu and Japan’s ABEMA.

body: “The Remarried Empress” has released a new set of palace stills featuring its four leads, offering a closer look at the characters at the heart of the fantasy romance.

Based on the web novel of the same name, the Disney+ series stars Shin Min Ah as Navier, empress of the Eastern Empire, and Ju Ji Hoon as her husband, Emperor Sovieshu. Their marriage falls apart when Sovieshu becomes involved with Rashta, a runaway slave played by Lee Se Young, and seeks a divorce. Navier responds by asking to marry Prince Heinrey, played by Lee Jong Suk.

The images, unveiled on November 9, include a portrait of Navier and Sovieshu standing together in a green garden, recalling their days as the empire’s ideal couple. Other stills show Navier in the palace and outdoors in the sunlight, while Sovieshu appears on horseback in a forest.
Heinrey is pictured against gardens and architecture, with a serious expression contrasting with his relaxed bearing. Rashta, meanwhile, wears brightly colored dresses with detailed embellishments.
The series premiered with four episodes on November 3. Two new episodes are scheduled to arrive each Wednesday, for a total of 10.

body: Kim Woo Bin is heading to the baseball field in “GIFT,” a new tvN sports drama that puts the value of natural talent and hard work up for debate.

A newly released teaser opens with his character, Jung Min Yong, outlining two paths to victory: an inborn gift for baseball and the detailed skills a player develops through effort. Yoon Seo Jin, played by Seo Eun Soo, asks which approach offers the better chance of winning.

items.headline: Seven GOING SEVENTEEN Picks, From Water Battles to a Zombie Escape
items.dek: Soompi’s latest watch list highlights seven SEVENTEEN variety-show adventures for fans looking for laughs, games and a few scares.
body: SEVENTEEN have taken on everything from deceptive quizzes to zombies on GOING SEVENTEEN. In a new watch list, Soompi recommends seven installments that show the range of the group’s variety series.

“Going Rangers” flips the superhero premise: the members compete to avoid becoming the universe’s savior. The cast and production crew join in the comedy, with moments including a spider dance and a Pikachu impression.
For fans who prefer strategy, “LIAR LIAR” turns a quiz into a contest of deception. Rather than simply getting answers right, the members try to mislead one another about what is true.

“SEVENTEEN TV” brings the group into a trainee-style dorm for a two-part series made as part of promotions for their 10th-anniversary album, HAPPY BURSTDAY. The members play exaggerated characters as they reenact trainee life.

In “MC BOO’s Dangerous Invitation,” Seungkwan interviews DK while the other members face a watery penalty whenever DK says an assigned forbidden word. Once he catches on, DK starts repeating the trigger words.

“WATER BATTLEGROUNDS” sends the members into a water-gun survival game, while “Mafiapoly” combines mafia and Monopoly with three members absent. Viewers sensitive to first-person camera footage may want to take care with “WATER BATTLEGROUNDS.”
The final pick, “TRAP,” trades games for horror: the members must escape an abandoned hospital while trying to avoid zombies. Handheld and distant camera shots add to the unsettling atmosphere.

items.headline: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Directors Join Animated Short ‘Living With a Visionary’
items.dek: Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans have joined Stephen P. Neary's animated documentary short as executive producers, ahead of its premiere through The New York Times Op-Docs.
body: Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, the directors behind KPop Demon Hunters, have joined the animated documentary short Living With a Visionary as executive producers. The short, narrated by James Cromwell, premieres through The New York Times Op-Docs this week.

Written, directed and animated by Stephen P. Neary, the film adapts a memoir by poet John Matthias. It follows his decades-long marriage to art curator Diana Matthias and how their life together shifts after her Parkinson's diagnosis, including the vivid hallucinations brought on by her medication, which John, now her caregiver, learns to live with alongside her.

Neary made the film with producer Mireia Vilanova, drawing thousands of illustrations by hand on layered vellum over three years, working on it during evenings and weekends around a full-time job and a teaching post at the California Institute of the Arts. The short has already picked up the grand jury prize for animation at AFI Fest and the short film jury award for animation at Sundance earlier this year.

Neary previously created and ran The Fungies! for Cartoon Network and HBO Max, supervised production on the Annie-nominated Clarence, and worked as a story artist on KPop Demon Hunters, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs, Rio and The Peanuts Movie. Kang and Appelhans said they were drawn to the project despite how different it looks from their own film, and Neary said the two projects share the same concerns underneath. Living With a Visionary is one of nine titles on Op-Docs' 2026 slate being talked about as awards contenders.

body: TOMORROW X TOGETHER has unveiled the first dates for its ‘STEAL THE WIND’ world tour, starting with three concerts in Seoul from November 13 to 15, 2026.

According to the official trailer released by HYBE LABELS, all three Seoul shows will also be available online. They are scheduled to begin at 7 p.m. KST on November 13, 6 p.m. on November 14 and 5 p.m. on November 15.

The tour will continue in Macau from November 20 to 22, before heading to Japan for shows in Fukuoka on December 19 and 20. Four more Japanese cities are on the schedule in 2027: Tokyo on January 7 and 8, Osaka on January 30 and 31, and Aichi on February 20 and 21.
March dates include Kaohsiung on March 6 and 7, Kuala Lumpur on March 13 and Jakarta on March 20.
In May, the group is scheduled to perform in Tacoma, Inglewood, Mexico City, Fort Worth, Atlanta, Belmont Park and Chicago. The run starts on May 4 in Tacoma and ends on May 25 in Chicago.
The European dates begin June 2 in Manchester and continue through Milan, Paris, Amsterdam and Antwerp before a June 14 show in Cologne. Hong Kong shows follow on June 19 and 20.
The trailer also indicates that more dates are to come. The tour schedule is available on the official TOMORROW X TOGETHER website.

items.headline: Nam Ji Hyun and Kim Jae Yeong Share Final Filming Memories in ‘Make Me Tingle’ Video
items.dek: A new behind-the-scenes video follows the stars through romantic rehearsals and their closing remarks as the drama wraps.
body: Nam Ji Hyun and Kim Jae Yeong are saying goodbye to “Make Me Tingle” in a new behind-the-scenes video from episodes 9 and 10.

The making-of footage shows the actors rehearsing romantic scenes, including a moment involving couple rings. During the rehearsal, the director laughs at Nam Ji Hyun’s surprised reaction, while Kim Jae Yeong jokes that she should accept quickly because of the cold.

Nam Ji Hyun suggests that they link arms, but Kim Jae Yeong slips his hands into his pockets to keep warm. Laughing, she proposes that they hold hands instead. He later shows off the couple rings to the making-of camera, joking that he has no money left.
The video also captures the pair taking photo booth pictures and cooking together, with their affectionate moments bringing smiles to the cast.

During their closing remarks, Kim Jae Yeong pretends to cry, making Nam Ji Hyun laugh. He says the drama was his second project with her and that he was fond of it, adding that he was happy they had wrapped up on an enjoyable note.

Nam Ji Hyun says she was relieved that everyone finished filming without getting sick, noting how much colder it had become since filming began. She also credits Kim Jae Yeong with making the set fun and helping her laugh throughout the shoot.

items.headline: Lee Joon Gi and Sakaguchi Kentaro Face New Clues in ‘kiDnap GAME’
items.dek: New stills preview another threat for detective Niide Toshiro as the thriller reveals a possible link to doctor Han Ki Joo.
body: Channel A’s “kiDnap GAME” has released new stills ahead of episode 6, as its survival game takes another turn for characters played by Lee Joon Gi and Sakaguchi Kentaro.

The thriller follows seven people caught in a kidnapping case spanning Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, Singapore, Bangkok, Naha and Manila. Each participant must complete a different mission ahead of the others to survive and save a loved one.

In the previous episode, objects found near eliminated participants added another layer to the mystery. A one-peso coin was placed in the hand of the granddaughter of Manila participant Miguel Garcia, played by Joel Torre, after he failed to prepare 10 million pesos in cash.

Bangkok participant Am Thanawan, played by Narupornkamol Chaisang, failed to expose a drug cartel; bread soaked in wine was used to gag her lover. Lipstick was also found on the lips of the deceased husband of Taipei participant Christina Lin, played by Alice Ko, after she failed to release a private video.

The objects connect to images in the show’s opening sequence: gold coins, a wine glass and a red apple. The ending scenes have shown the coins, glass or apple being destroyed or decaying when a participant is eliminated. Red rose petals have also been left alongside the clues.

The series is beginning to reveal how some participants may be connected. Seoul doctor Han Ki Joo, played by Lee Joon Gi, remembers an incident in Tokyo five years earlier after seeing Christina’s son. Han had been working at a Tokyo hospital at the time and treated a child with burn injuries.
Tokyo detective Niide Toshiro, played by Sakaguchi Kentaro, also reacts to the reference to Tokyo five years ago, suggesting a connection between the two men.

A young man played by Sho Kasamatsu adds to the uncertainty. After ambushing Niide’s junior detective, he appears at a Tokyo broadcasting station and offers reporter Isobe Akina, played by Sae Okazaki, an exclusive story.
Meanwhile, Niide is in Taipei when the perpetrator sends him a message saying a new stage has been prepared for him. Episode 6 airs November 10 at 10 p.m. KST.

source.title: 6 Workplace C-Dramas Where Women Took Charge

items.headline: 6 Chinese Workplace Dramas About Women Finding Their Own Paths
items.dek: From consulting to law and entrepreneurship, these dramas follow women balancing career ambitions with personal challenges.
body: Workplace dramas can put more than office rivalries in the spotlight. These six Chinese series follow women making decisions about their careers, relationships and futures, whether they are navigating a demanding employer or starting a business of their own.

The Rational Life
Qin Lan plays Shen Ruo Xin, a senior manager in an automobile company’s legal department who faces gender discrimination at work and pressure to marry at home. When optimistic intern Qi Xiao (Dylan Wang) enters her life, his support prompts her to reconsider her views on relationships while she continues to make choices for herself.

Nothing But Thirty
Set in Shanghai, this drama follows three women as they enter their thirties. Luxury saleswoman Wang Man Ni (Maggie Jiang) hopes to build a better life, Gu Jia (Tong Yao) balances family responsibilities with helping run her husband’s fireworks business, and Zhong Xiao Qin (Mao Xiao Tong) reassesses her choices amid marital difficulties. Their intersecting stories explore ambition, financial independence and friendship.

Irreplaceable
Zhao Jin Mai stars as Xu Chi, a newcomer determined to prove herself in the competitive consulting industry. Elite consultant Ye Xin Zhi (Wei Da Xun), who is dealing with the fallout of a former superior’s betrayal, becomes her mentor. Their relationship develops alongside workplace rivalries and career challenges.

As Beautiful As You
After growing frustrated with her job, technology professional Ji Xing (Tan Song Yun) leaves to launch a medical technology start-up. Building the company brings setbacks, but she eventually gains the backing of investor Han Ting (Xu Kai). Their partnership turns romantic, even as Ji Xing remains intent on pursuing her goals on her own terms.

Love Has Fireworks
Investment banker Qian Fei (Wang Chu Ran) must rethink her future after her fiancé leaves her and she is left with a mortgage. She rents a room to Li Yi Fei (Tan Jian Ci), another investment banking professional, to ease the financial strain. The pair initially clash, but grow closer as they share a home and work on projects together.

She and Her Perfect Husband
Career-focused lawyer Qin Shi (Yang Mi) becomes a candidate for a position at a law firm that requires applicants to be married, unaware that her brother has falsely listed her as a wife. She later meets Yang Hua (Xu Kai), and the two agree to marry. Their arrangement brings professional and family pressures into focus as their relationship develops.

source.title: CORTIS, Stray Kids, NMIXX, SEVENTEEN’s JxJ, K/DA, ILLIT, ENHYPEN, BTS, And More Sweep Top Spots On Billboard World Albums Chart

items.headline: CORTIS Returns to No. 1 on Billboard World Albums Chart as NMIXX and JxJ Debut
items.dek: GREENGREEN leads the chart for a sixth week, while new releases from NMIXX, SEVENTEEN’s JxJ, K/DA and ILLIT enter the top 10.
body: CORTIS is back at No. 1 on Billboard’s World Albums chart for the week ending November 7. The group’s EP “GREENGREEN” returned to the top for its sixth week in the position and re-entered the Billboard 200 six months after its release.
CORTIS also charted with debut EP “COLOR OUTSIDE THE LINES,” which placed No. 22 in its 60th week on the World Albums chart.
Stray Kids held three spots, led by “THIS & THAT” at No. 2 in its 12th week. “KARMA” ranked No. 9 in its 59th week, while “DO IT” came in at No. 18 in its 41st.
Two new releases followed at Nos. 3 and 4: NMIXX’s EP “Strange Muse” and “DREAMSCAPE,” the debut mini album from SEVENTEEN unit JxJ, made up of Jeonghan and Joshua.

ENHYPEN’s “THE SIN : BLISS” placed No. 5 in its 10th week. League of Legends virtual group K/DA debuted at No. 6 with “FIRESTARTER,” while ILLIT’s “BREAK EVEN” entered at No. 7 ahead of its U.S. physical release. ILLIT’s earlier mini album “MAMIHLAPINATAPAI” ranked No. 13 in its 26th week.
BTS also had two albums on the chart: “Map of the Soul: 7 ~The Journey~” at No. 12 and “Love Yourself: Answer,” which re-entered at No. 15 for its 206th week.

Further down, ATEEZ’s “GOLDEN HOUR : Part.5” ranked No. 16, followed by NewJeans’ “Get Up” at No. 17 and BOYNEXTDOOR’s “HOME” at No. 19. LE SSERAFIM’s “PUREFLOW” placed No. 21, and EVAN (Heeseung)’s “DEATH OF ME” came in at No. 24.

items.headline: The Philippine K-pop Concert Guide: Every 2026–2027 Show, Venue and Ticket Link
items.dek: Fourteen K-pop shows are headed to the Philippines from November 2026 to March 2027, from HUTA's Heat Max to three sold-out BTS nights in Bulacan. Here is every date, venue and official ticket link in one place.
body: Fourteen K-pop concerts are on the calendar for the Philippines between November 2026 and March 2027, and the HallyuScope concert calendar tracks every one of them — with the poster, seat plan and official ticket link for each show. Here is the full rundown, month by month.

November opens with LEE MINHYUK (HUTA), who brings his HEAT MAX tour to the SM North EDSA Skydome in Quezon City on November 21, then PENTAGON's 10th anniversary tour, 101010, at the Aliw Theater in Pasay on November 29. Both shows are on sale through Ticketmaster Philippines. One date fans should cross off: OMEGA X's November 28 Manila show was cancelled in September, and the promoter is processing refunds.

December has a genuine clash. PARK JINYOUNG plays his first concert tour, CODE, at the FYM Hall in the EVM Convention Center, Quezon City, on December 5, and LE SSERAFIM plays the SM Mall of Asia Arena the same night — both at 7:00 PM, so it is a one-or-the-other decision. LE SSERAFIM's December 6 show was cancelled and its ticket holders were moved to December 5. NCT 127 closes the month with NEO CITY — THE REDLINE at the MOA Arena on December 12 at 5:00 PM.

January brings three different flavours. JACOB of THE BOYZ plays his More Than Words fan concert at the Music Museum in San Juan on January 19 at 8:00 PM, DOH KYUNG SOO brings his DAY OFF fan concert to the Smart Araneta Coliseum on January 23 at 6:00 PM — tickets go on sale November 20 at 2:00 PM through TicketNet — and KATSEYE's Beautiful Chaos world tour reaches the MOA Arena on January 29. The Manila date is already sold out on Ticketmaster, so the Cebu stop is the one to watch.

February is the month of the double booking. KATSEYE plays the SM Seaside Cebu Arena on February 7, and on February 20 BIGBANG returns to the Philippines for the first time since 2015 with XX: COSMOS at the SMDC Festival Grounds in Parañaque, while Young K of DAY6 plays The Youngest at the New Frontier Theater in Quezon City the same night at 6:00 PM.

March belongs to BTS. The group's ARIRANG world tour plays three nights at the Philippine Sports Stadium in Bulacan — March 13, 14 and 16 — and all three are sold out. The March 16 date was added after the first two sold out in June 2026.

Two things worth knowing before you buy. First, every ticket link on the HallyuScope concert calendar goes to the official seller for that show — Ticketmaster Philippines, SM Tickets, TicketNet, Tap Your Tickets or Megatix — so a link that is not on the calendar is not one we have verified. Second, prices and statuses change: the ranges in this guide are the prices as announced, and the calendar is updated as shows sell out, move or are added.
